text:
built a full self-driving wheelchair.

hit summon on the ipad and it drives itself over to you, or just say "take me to the blue sofa" and it takes you there. an arduino pretends to be the joystick so we didn't cut a single wire, and our post-trained omnivla model drives it off a phone camera.

built with urjit chakraborty, yaseen moustafa, and ibraheem shaikh.
alt: An empty electric wheelchair driving itself across a room toward a person on a couch, with the model's camera view and the iPad app shown in the corners.

text:
nimbotics.net is up.

one robot learns a skill in simulation, saves what worked, and every other robot can pick it up, even ones built completely differently.
alt: Nimbotics: One robot learns it. Every robot remembers. A robot arm drawn in points of light.

text:
helix won bloomberg's most philanthropic hack.

pick a cancer type and a protein target and it pulls 14,000 real compounds from chembl, scores them with ml models trained on actual lab experiments, and surfaces the top 10 in seconds. then each candidate gets checked with vqe, a real quantum algorithm, for molecular stability.

everything in it comes from real data. drug discovery doesn't have room for fake precision.

built with bassil shalaby and reyan yousif.
alt: Adam with teammates and Bloomberg judges after winning Most Philanthropic Hack for Helix.

text:
immortal won best healthcare hack at anthropic.

wearables collect tons of health data but don't help you do anything with it. you can see your hrv drop, but not why or what to change. immortal learns your personal baselines, catches meaningful changes, and turns them into evidence-backed recommendations with real citations.

the best part is self-experiments: try something like cutting caffeine after 2pm and it tracks the before and after and tells you if it actually worked.

built with shanmukha pothukuchi, reyan yousif, and bassil shalaby.
alt: Adam with Shanmukha, Reyan and Bassil holding the Best Healthcare Hack award for Immortal.
